policy_name: Ars Technica’s policy on generative AI
country_region: Global (Ars Technica newsroom, United States-based publication)
geo_constraints: All editorial work produced by Ars Technica's writers, editors and contributors

locale_context.regulation: Self-regulation · newsroom editorial standard, published for readers
locale_context.culture: US technology-journalism newsroom ethics: human authorship, source verification and editorial accountability, made public as a reader-trust commitment rather than a compliance document.

key_dates.event: Policy last updated (as printed at end of policy)

versions.title: Ars Technica’s policy on generative AI (last updated 22 April 2026)
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.

covered_entities: Ars Technica writers, editors and contributors
covered_systems: generative AI tools for text, research, images, audio and video
AI-powered editing aids (grammar, style, structural feedback)
covered_activities: production of images, audio and video
exceptions: AI output reproduced as the subject of reporting (set apart and disclosed)
standard production edits (color correction, cropping, contrast)
conditions: research assistance only with AI tools vetted and approved for the workflow
objective: Tell readers how Ars Technica does and does not use generative AI: journalism stays human-authored, AI-assisted research is verified, attributions come from direct sourcing, synthetic media is never passed off as real, and people stay accountable.

sources_consulted: https://arstechnica.com/ai-policy/ (URL printed in the document; not fetched)
record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/ars.md). The copy combines an introductory post by Ken Fisher with the policy itself; clauses are taken from the policy part only. The policy states it was last updated April 22, 2026; no first-publication or effective date is given (the intro says the standards have governed editorial work since AI tooling became available, and the reader-facing version is a translation of an internal policy), so effective_date is null. The document says changes will be noted on the policy page; not checked whether a later update exists. binding=false; the standards are mandatory for Ars editorial staff and contributors ('When violations occur, we take action').

clauses.original_text: Ars Technica’s editorial text is written by humans. We do not use AI to generate our reporting, analysis, or commentary.
clauses.actor: Ars Technica writers, editors and contributors
clauses.requirement: editorial text is human-written; AI is not used to generate journalism
clauses.exception: AI output reproduced as exemplar material when AI is the subject of reporting
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools used in Ars Technica's editorial workflow
clauses.interpretation_notes: Exception: AI output may be reproduced when it is itself the subject of reporting, set apart and disclosed; AI editing aids (grammar, style, structure) may recommend but not make changes.

clauses.original_text: AI tools must not be used to generate, extract, or summarize material that is then attributed to a named source, whether as a direct quote, a paraphrase, or a characterization of someone’s views.
clauses.object: material attributed to a named source
clauses.requirement: attributed quotes, paraphrases and characterisations must come from direct engagement with the source material
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools used in Ars Technica's editorial workflow
clauses.interpretation_notes: Attributed material must come from interviews, transcripts, published statements or documents reviewed by the reporter.

clauses.original_text: Even then, AI output is never treated as an authoritative source. Everything must be verified. … We don’t publish claims based solely on AI-generated summaries, and reporters may not represent any material as “reviewed” unless they have examined it directly.
clauses.requirement: verify all AI research output; no claims based solely on AI summaries
clauses.condition: when AI tools are used to assist research
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools vetted and approved for the Ars workflow (research, summarising, dataset search)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Research use is limited to tools vetted and approved for the workflow.

clauses.original_text: Every author who uses AI tools in the course of reporting a story must disclose that use to their editors, and authors remain fully responsible for their content.
clauses.object: use of AI tools in reporting
clauses.requirement: internal disclosure of AI use to editors; author retains full responsibility
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools used in Ars Technica's editorial workflow
clauses.interpretation_notes: Internal (to editors), not reader-facing, disclosure. Section 'Accountability is non-negotiable' adds that responsibility cannot be transferred to colleagues, editors or tools.

clauses.original_text: We do not publish AI-generated images, audio, or video as authentic documentation of real events. We do not alter documentary media in ways that change their meaning.
clauses.actor: Ars Technica editorial and art teams
clauses.requirement: no synthetic media presented as real; no meaning-changing edits to documentary media
clauses.exception: standard production work such as color correction, cropping and contrast adjustments
clauses.purpose: prevent misleading the public about real events
clauses.applicable_systems: image, audio and video generation tools
clauses.interpretation_notes: Standard production work (colour correction, cropping, contrast) is expressly allowed.

clauses.original_text: When synthetic media is used in the context of reporting on AI, it will be clearly identified as AI-generated, with that disclosure placed as close to the material as possible.
clauses.object: synthetic media used in reporting on AI
clauses.requirement: clear AI-generated label placed next to the material
clauses.condition: when synthetic media is used in reporting on AI
clauses.interpretation_notes: Framed as 'will be' (a commitment); treated as mandatory.
